[REFERENCE] 7. No significant past medical history.

[QUERY] How old is the patient?

[THOUGHT] An 18-month-old unvaccinated child with 2 days of fever and a pruritic rash that began on the trunk and spread to face and extremities is most consistent with primary varicella infection (chickenpox). The distribution (trunk-first with spread), age, lack of varicella immunization or prior illness, and pruritus strongly favor varicella over measles, roseola, or drug exanthem. Although lesion morphology was not definitively reported, the clinical setting provides sufficient likelihood to make varicella the single most likely diagnosis.

[DIAGNOSIS] Varicella (chickenpox)
